sections.h2: Filing a deed in Meigs County
sections.html:
Deeds for Meigs County land are filed at the recorder's office, 100 E. Second Street, Pomeroy, Ohio 45769. The office keeps weekday hours of eight in the morning to four in the afternoon. Anything that conveys, mortgages or otherwise burdens a parcel gets a permanent entry in its records.

Sellers should care about that entry because a title company reads it before closing. An old mortgage, a lien or a gap in the chain of owners has to be cleared first, or the buyer cannot take clean title.

When you go in person, bring the signed deed, the auditor's receipt for the conveyance fee and a check or cash for the recording total. Call first for the exact amount, since it depends on page count and on any references to earlier documents.

Recording charges are fixed by Ohio law, and the Ohio Recorders' Association publishes the schedule. Each fee splits evenly between the recorder and the state's Housing Trust Fund. Counties may also add a preservation surcharge capped at five dollars, so ask the Meigs office whether it applies before you write a check.

Standard Ohio recording fees
Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage, lease, easement or land contract, first two pages$34.00
Each additional page$8.00
Release, assignment or affidavit that references a prior documentBase fee plus $4.00 per reference
Document that fails the state format rules$20.00
Federal tax lien$5.00
Military dischargeNo fee

Copy charges differ from county to county. Call the Meigs office for its price on plain and certified copies.

sections.h2: The conveyance fee on a sale
sections.html:
The conveyance fee, often called the transfer tax, goes to the auditor and not the recorder. The auditor charges $4.00 for each thousand dollars of price, on houses and manufactured homes alike.

The auditor's paperwork includes DTE Form 100 (statement of value and receipt) and DTE Form 100EX (exemption). Form 101 covers the conveyance of homestead property. Conveyance standards dated July 1, 2025 are posted on the auditor's site, and a surveyor or attorney should read them before drafting a legal description.

A used manufactured home sold after January 1, 2000 must be transferred through the auditor, who adds a 50-cent transfer fee. Once the conveyance is paid, the clerk of courts can move the title with no sales tax.

sections.h2: How values are set and contested
sections.html:
The auditor values real property at the price it would bring in an arm's-length sale. Staff review permits, land splits and boundary surveys, and they inspect new construction.

Disputes go to the Board of Revision. The auditor serves as its permanent secretary, with the county treasurer and the president of the commissioners. Get the complaint form (DTE Form 1) from the auditor's office, and file it by March 31 each year.

Owners who live in their house can also seek the 2.5 percent tax reduction. The auditor applies three tests:

  • the applicant owns the home;
  • it is the applicant's main residence;
  • the application is filed between January 1 and the first Monday in June.

Rentals, corporate or partnership owners and acreage past the first acre do not qualify.

sections.h2: Meigs County housing and local market
sections.html:
Meigs County had 21,587 people in July 2025, a drop of 2.8 percent since the 2020 count. About three of every four households (75.4 percent) own their home, out of 9,102 households. The 2020 census found 10,649 housing units and a 13.6 percent vacancy rate, so roughly one home in seven stood empty then.

  • The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $119,300.
  • Owners with a mortgage report $1,130 a month in costs, and those without one report $473.
  • Renters pay $722 at the median.
  • Household income is $46,873 at the median.
  • No building permits were recorded for the county in 2025.

Low values and little new construction mean a seller's price often rests on a few nearby sales. Expect buyers to ask about the condition of older homes.

Coal mining, strip and underground, left its mark on Meigs County from the late nineteenth century onward. Anyone selling land over old workings should read the auditor's posted guide, Developing on Abandoned Mine Land, before listing.

The Meigs County Auditor keeps a separate page on manufactured homes. Homes bought after January 1, 2000 are taxed like real property under the appraisal method, with values reset every three years at 35 percent of estimated market value. Older homes may stay on the depreciation method or make a one-time switch to the appraisal method after all taxes are paid.

  • Owners must register a home with the auditor within 30 days of locating it in the county, and a failure to register can bring a $100 fine.
  • A relocation notice, required to move a home on a public road, costs $5 at the auditor's office and requires that taxes be paid.
  • A home on a permanent foundation on land the owner also owns may qualify to be taxed as real estate after the title is inactivated and surrendered.

If you plan to sell a manufactured home that has moved or changed tax methods, call the auditor first so the transfer paperwork matches the home's status.

The county tax map office now runs its own website at meigscountytaxmap.com. Land splits and boundary surveys go through the tax map department before the auditor reviews them for new values, so a seller dividing a parcel should start there. Ask that office for its current requirements before you order a survey.

sections.h2: Papers recorded when a house changes hands
sections.html:
Most sales involve a deed and, if the seller owed money, a mortgage release. Each one is recorded on its own and priced by page. A release or assignment also carries the per-reference charge shown in the table above.

  • Warranty or fiduciary deed from seller to buyer.
  • Mortgage release recorded after payoff.
  • Affidavit or court certificate when an estate is the seller.

If the lender has started a foreclosure, the auditor's page points owners to the county sheriff's website at meigssheriff.org for the list of upcoming sheriff's sales.

Before closing, ask your title company for a list of everything it plans to record and a total for the page count. Then you can check the figure against the table above and avoid a surprise at the signing. A cash buyer needs no new mortgage recorded, so the packet is usually shorter.

faqs.q: What is the address and phone number for the Meigs County Recorder?
faqs.a: The office is at 100 E. Second Street, Pomeroy, Ohio 45769, and it keeps weekday hours of eight to four. Call ahead to confirm hours before a trip.

faqs.q: How much does Meigs County charge for filing a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule is $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each added page. A county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5. Call the recorder to get the exact total for your page count.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance fee on a Meigs County sale?
faqs.a: The county auditor charges $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price for both real estate and manufactured homes. A 50-cent transfer fee also applies to manufactured homes. Ask the auditor which form your deed needs.

faqs.q: When must a Meigs County valuation complaint be filed?
faqs.a: By March 31 of the year you are contesting. File it with the county auditor, who is secretary of the Board of Revision. Forms are available from the auditor's office.

faqs.q: Does recording a military discharge cost anything in Meigs County?
faqs.a: No. Ohio sets no fee for recording a military discharge, and the fee schedule shows it as free.
